distractors: Placed first in a sequence of steps, so that everything after it depends on it being done.
Handled personally by the most senior person available rather than delegated down to whoever happens to have capacity that week.
Settled before any other item on the agenda can be discussed, because nothing that follows it makes sense until it is. It is a claim about sequence and about what blocks what.

Kept visible only to the people who actually need it and closed to everyone else, so that a sensitive number does not travel further than intended. The control is on the audience, and it is set deliberately.

Turned to face the customer rather than the back office, naming the part of a business a client actually touches: the people, the screens, the paperwork they sign. Everything behind that line is someone else's problem to run, and it is staffed and priced differently.
